subject: business-studies
title: Quality Management: TQM and Six Sigma
welcome_lead: From inspection to TQM to Six Sigma - quality is everyone's job.
meta_desc: A-Level Operations: TQM, Six Sigma, quality control vs assurance.
final_note: Build quality in, do not inspect it in after the fact.

concepts.def: Checking finished products to catch defects.

walkthroughs.body_html: Quality control reacts - inspectors at the end of the line. Quality assurance prevents - designing the process so defects do not happen. The latter is cheaper at scale.
TQM embeds quality in culture. Every employee - not just QA - is responsible. It demands training, empowerment and clear metrics; the payoff is fewer defects and stronger brand trust.
Six Sigma uses the DMAIC cycle (Define, Measure, Analyse, Improve, Control) to drive defect rates down to 3.4 per million. Pioneered by Motorola and adopted by GE.

options: Operations management is the same as general management.
